I was watching "True Detective" the other night (s2e6) and the state police were having a disagreement with the local cops and the federal park police (or something) about whose crime scene it was and who gets to work the case. And they were being real dicks to each other too - like they've been having this same argument for years and absolutely hate each other. Then it occurred to me that almost every movie or TV show about police investigations does this every single time. There's a murder and the FBI and local cops argue and fight about who gets to gather the evidence and make decisions and what-not. Hell, sometimes it's even within the same department (like homicide vs narcotics, etc.). And it isn't a civil discussion/debate like you might have in an office or something - the various sides are very sarcastic to each other, hurling insults and trying to one-up the other side; sometimes even making threats. Do you guys/gals really have these "jurisdiction" disputes and if so, are they generally as heated as if they are the Hatfields and the McCoys? If not, why does TV/movies do this? It's funny because in my experience we usually fight about who HAS to take the case and not who GETS to take it. As soon as we find out it happened in another jurisdiction, we ship it off. The exception to this would be narcotics cases. People are always undercutting each other on long term dope investigations and it doesn't help that snitches often work for multiple agencies and provide the same information to different departments.
